segments.text: Episode twenty-five. Next stop... the edge of the universe.
The universe is about thirteen point eight billion years old. But the edge of what we can see is much farther than thirteen point eight billion light-years.
segments.headline: Farther than you think

segments.text: Because space kept stretching while the light traveled, that edge is now about forty-six billion light-years away, in every direction.
That makes the observable universe about ninety-three billion light-years across.
Inside it, there are hundreds of billions of galaxies, maybe more.
segments.headline: Hundreds of billions of galaxies

segments.text: And beyond the edge? Almost certainly more universe. We just can't see it, because its light hasn't reached us yet.
segments.headline: What's beyond?

segments.text: That's the end of season one. Tomorrow, season two begins with the strangest worlds ever found. Next stop: a planet where it rains iron. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-six.
